tldr: Web-Bench is a new LLM code benchmark featuring 50 fullstack web development projects with 20 sequentially dependent tasks each, designed to address benchmark saturation by evaluating LLMs on real-world web standards and frameworks.
contributions: Proposes Web-Bench, a benchmark with 50 projects each containing 20 sequentially dependent tasks simulating real-world development workflows
Covers foundational web standards (CSS Selector, DOM, SVG, WebGL, ECMAScript, TypeScript) and frameworks (UI, State Management, CSS, Build, Fullstack, Database)
Demonstrates benchmark saturation in existing benchmarks and shows Web-Bench remains unsaturated with SOTA at only 25.1% Pass@1
methods: The benchmark contains 50 projects designed by engineers with 5-10 years of experience, each with 20 tasks having sequential dependencies (each task builds on prior task outputs). Tasks cover diverse business scenarios including Games, Charts, Drawing Boards, Blogs, and Data Tables. Evaluation uses end-to-end Playwright tests (average 3.6 cases per task, 72.4 per project) through a Web-Agent that builds prompts, requests LLM APIs, and extracts generated files, with up to 2 retry attempts using error context.
results: Claude 3.7 Sonnet achieves 25.1% Pass@1 on Web-Bench, lower than SWE-Bench Verified (65.4%) and Full (33.8%). Closed-source models average 15.08% Pass@1 and 20.79% Pass@2 vs. open models at 10.73% and 14.84% respectively. Newer or larger-parameter models within the same series generally perform better. HumanEval (99.4%) and MBPP (94.2%) are saturated, while Web-Bench remains far from saturation.
limitations: Evaluation cost is high—each project takes 4-8 hours for a senior engineer, suggesting significant computational overhead for benchmarking. A Lite version is planned for the future, indicating the current benchmark may be too resource-intensive for widespread use. The paper also notes aesthetics and code quality evaluation is left for future work.
